Revision 6 passed real-host and formal source preparation, enabled auto-forward, reached draft revision 48 and six workflow runs, then failed after 33 model calls and 92 tool calls because the runner left the daemon at its default thirty-turn token ceiling instead of projecting the frozen 120-turn task budget before session creation.

Revision 7 passed task-author preflight and correctly projected 120 turns, then consumed 103 model calls, 139 tools, 15,500,762 tokens, and eleven workflow runs before explicitly reporting that only 8/24 public records and an incomplete dry-run workflow existed; no capability report, host write, claim, or oracle result was produced.

A fresh-state retry of the same immutable revision reached 58 model calls, 73 tools, draft revision 19, three succeeded and one paused workflow runs, generated JSON and CSV artifacts for 24 public records, then ended its Builder turn while real XLSX, host writes, registered artifacts, publication, acceptance, capability report, claim, and oracle remained absent. Three exact workspace-write permissions were independently allowed. The daemon session was cancelled after the incomplete final summary, but formal collaboration authority closure remained pending and the empty runner poll was interrupted.

Revision 8 package preparation and real-host zero-write baseline passed. Before application creation, the task-local secret provisioning request reached stale revision 7 processes still bound to ports 18100/18101 and failed with invalid API token. The exact stale environment, platform, daemon, proxy, and attestation process groups were terminated; no host write, application, assignment, report, claim, or oracle was produced.

A fresh revision 8 assignment entered Builder execution and requested three exact task-local workspace writes. Two were allowed before the interrupted runner lifecycle exposed connection refresh races and a malformed daemon SQLite database on resume. The immutable waiting, assignment-failed, and resume-failed receipts remain in the attempt chain; no host write, formal report, claim, or oracle result was produced.

Another clean-state revision 8 run built a real draft and reached a task-local write request, but the platform rejected daemon event 707 after durable cursor 706 because the event payload contained a credential-shaped field. The platform assignment therefore remained stale while the local daemon waited on an unrelayed workspace_write for work/enterprise-result.json. The run was stopped instead of bypassing the formal relay or waiting three hours.

The latest user instruction authorizes unattended agent collaboration for the supplementation task. Revision 9 records that authority without expanding the frozen task: only exact workspace_write/workspace_patch requests inside work/artifacts can be automatically allowed; business Human Input, host 403 behavior, connectors, network, secrets, budget, oracle, and all other side-effect boundaries remain unchanged and fail-closed.

The fresh revision 9 run relayed and acknowledged all 1,418 daemon events, reached 49 model calls, 68 tools, 3,809,328 tokens, draft revision 28, and eight failed workflow runs, then terminated when DeepSeek returned HTTP 402 Insufficient Balance. Baseline and final host snapshots both contained 36 records and zero write requests. No operational permission was requested, so the unattended resolver remains deterministically verified but not yet exercised by a real Builder run.

Before replenishing provider balance, the user requested proof that no background workflow was consuming tokens and stage-level token monitoring. Revision 10 keeps real model egress fail-closed by default, requires an explicit per-run flag, and records read-only token/cost snapshots without changing the enterprise requirement or acceptance.
The first explicit post-recharge invocation omitted the local environment export and failed before starting the real-host environment or model. The immutable run_failed receipt is retained.

A fresh state root completed 101 model calls, 13,460,126 tokens, and multiple platform operations, but produced only a three-node demo-data workflow with no real host writes, XLSX, publication, formal claim, or independent oracle. Baseline and final snapshots remained 36 records with zero requests; the failed attempt is retained.

A second fresh state root reached 77 model calls and 11,459,315 tokens and built an eleven-node draft, but still made zero host requests and produced no XLSX, artifact receipt, or oracle result. Three collaboration reports failed local schema validation and no report was persisted; the platform correctly rejected a false and incomplete formal archive.

The formal report tool now exposes bounded public validation paths, types, and messages so Lilies can correct a report without seeing inputs, secrets, validation context, or URLs. The enterprise requirement, fixtures, oracle, budgets, and acceptance are unchanged; no CAP-LILIES entry exists until a project run submits and routes a complete reusable capability report.

The fresh revision 11 run completed 59 model calls, 8,081,074 tokens, draft revision 27, and seven workflow runs, but embedded public debug labels and fabricated success strings in a three-node workflow and treated one structural test as business completion. Baseline and final host snapshots each retained 36 records and zero requests. No registered artifact, host receipt, formal report, claim, archive, or oracle result was produced.

A formal model loop that ends without accepted durable completion evidence now receives exactly one persistent, deterministic, same-turn protocol continuation. It adds no authorization, does not change the task or acceptance, consumes the original cumulative budget and deadline, does not affect customer-mode sessions, and does not reveal any project-specific expected gap.

The fresh revision 12 seed-101 run reached 19 model calls, 41 tool calls, and 1,930,525 tokens before requesting an authorized workspace_write. The runner's deterministic permission idempotency key concatenated the task ID, request UUID, and full input digest into more than the bridge schema's 128-character maximum, so the platform correctly rejected the automatic decision with 422. Baseline and final host snapshots each retained 36 records and zero requests; no report, artifact, claim, archive, or oracle result was produced.
